result.summary: Runs a scripted diff across test and benchmark files to explicitly include `util/check.h` in files that invoke `assert` or `Assert`, removing redundant `<cassert>` includes. A second scripted commit sorts the modified includes using `clang-format-diff.py`.
result.problem: Test code uses assertions without consistently including `util/check.h`, creating confusion over whether assertions might be disabled by `NDEBUG` or whether `assert` or `Assert` is intended. It also complicates automated Include-What-You-Use (IWYU) analysis.
evidence: Author states in the commit message that 'The project has a compile error when compiled without assertions in util/check.h. Thus, util/check.h should be included for all assertions.'
Author notes in the description that the change avoids assertion confusion and 'will also make it easier to run IWYU.'
result.scope_notes: Purely mechanical scripted diff affecting 57 test and benchmark files.
result.card: Runs scripted diffs to ensure test and benchmark files using assert or Assert include util/check.h and remove direct cassert includes, then sorts the modified headers. This aims to avoid confusion over NDEBUG assertion disabling and aid Include-What-You-Use (IWYU) tooling. The author notes that the project fails to compile without assertions in util/check.h, though no external issues or dependencies are specified.

risk.why: Touches only includes within test and benchmark files, where a mistake would only cause compilation failures in tests.
